prompt: Radians measure an angle by the ARC LENGTH you walk around the unit circle. Half a turn is $\pi$ radians. How many degrees is $\pi$ radians?
hint: Half of a full turn. A full turn is $360^\circ$.

hints.text: Half of a full turn. A full turn is $360^\circ$.
$\pi$ radians $= 180^\circ$. This is the swap rule you will use again and again.

explanation: Walking all the way around a circle of radius $1$ covers an arc of $2\pi$, so a full turn is $2\pi$ radians.
Half of that walk is $\pi$ radians, and half of a full turn is $360 \div 2 = 180^\circ$.
So $\pi$ radians $= 180^\circ$. Radians and degrees are two rulers measuring the same turn.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two rulers, one turn
steps: Think of measuring a table in inches or centimetres. Same table, two numbers.
Degrees chop a full turn into 360 pieces. Radians measure the same turn by arc length: 2π all the way round, so π is halfway = 180°.

alternativeExplanations.title: Walk it out
steps: Start at the far right of the unit circle and walk counter-clockwise along the rim.
When you have walked an arc of length π you are at the far LEFT — directly opposite where you started. Opposite means half a turn, which is 180°.
